chain.title: Choose a local cable network
chain.desc: Craft networking cable and keep each local network's cable color consistent. Different colors can help separate adjacent networks without changing what resources a channel carries.

chain.title: Attach a machine to the network
chain.desc: Place a connector against a compatible inventory, fluid tank, or energy block. Use matching cable to reach the controller and name important endpoints clearly.

chain.title: Program the first channels
chain.desc: Power the XNet Controller and inspect the detected connectors. Add a channel of the intended resource type, then configure its extraction and insertion endpoints.

chain.title: Move a test stack through XNet
chain.desc: Connect two inventories, create an item channel, and configure one endpoint to extract and the other to insert. Confirm after a test stack reaches the intended destination.

chain.title: Give fluids their own channel
chain.desc: Connect suitable tanks or machines and configure a fluid channel with the correct extraction and insertion settings. Confirm after a test fluid reaches its destination without mixing unintended fluids.

chain.title: Supply a machine through a channel
chain.desc: Configure an energy channel from an existing source to a compatible consumer. Keep the controller itself powered, then confirm after the target machine receives energy.

chain.title: Upgrade a chosen endpoint
chain.desc: Craft a Connector Upgrade for an endpoint that needs the advanced connector's capabilities. Upgrade the connection that limits the route rather than every idle endpoint.

chain.title: Configure advanced transfer
chain.desc: Use an Advanced Connector where the setup needs its additional transfer or side-selection features. Recheck channel settings after replacing or upgrading a connector.

chain.title: Expose a redstone-controlled block
chain.desc: Use a Redstone Proxy where the network needs the supported redstone interaction with another block. Test the target behavior before letting it switch a larger machine system.

chain.title: Separate routing from local cables
chain.desc: Craft routing cable for a network that connects routers and published channels. Routing cable has a different job from the colored local network cable.

chain.title: Join a routing endpoint
chain.desc: Use Routing Connectors for the router network and keep local machine connections on their controller networks. Name the networks before publishing shared channels.

chain.title: Share selected channels between networks
chain.desc: Connect a Router to the routing network and publish or consume the intended channels. Start with one shared route and verify the endpoints before joining several factory networks.

chain.title: Prepare the wireless structure
chain.desc: Build the antenna base components required by the supported wireless setup. Review the antenna arrangement before choosing a wireless router location.

chain.title: Give the wireless router an antenna
chain.desc: Construct the supported antenna on the wireless router. Its tier and arrangement determine the available wireless reach; the router block alone is not the complete setup.

chain.title: Link separate factory networks
chain.desc: Configure Wireless Routers and the required antennas to publish and consume intended channels. Verify network names, range, and loaded endpoints before relying on a remote supply line.

chain.title: Expand the wireless branch
chain.desc: Build the higher-tier antenna arrangement using the dish and required supporting blocks. Check the installed range and dimension behavior instead of assuming every antenna connects everywhere.

chain.title: Finish the cable route
chain.desc: Use facades on supported network blocks to fit the room's design. Confirm the underlying connections still work before covering the completed route.

coverage.scope: Authored branched progression; item and component acquisition objectives, not automatic proof that a factory works.
limits: Different cable colors are alternatives, not separate progression tiers.
Channel configuration milestones use player confirmation; inventory detection cannot prove a configured route.
Pack scripts, recipe changes, and other Minecraft versions require the installed-pack scan; this guide is not a complete mod manual.
coverage.verification: Local JAR item models and English registry names; selected recipes and bundled manuals checked. Not a new in-game playthrough.

notes: Re-reviewed 2026-10-07 against local Minecraft 1.20.1 JAR item assets and selected recipes/manuals, with official project sources listed separately. Every authored row now has explicit prerequisites; empty lists identify intentional branch roots. The coverage section states the verified versions and remaining limits. This replaces older list-order and item-count claims.
